summary: Russian forces conducted a large-scale overnight drone offensive on 30-31 October 2026, striking Kyiv's TEC-6 thermal power plant with at least three Geran-5 drones causing widespread power and water outages, while dozens of reactive UAVs penetrated airspace across Sumy, Poltava, Chernihiv, Kyiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Simultaneously, Russian forces executed a double strike on Dnipro's energy infrastructure and railway station, damaging a substation and generating a large smoke column. A ballistic missile launch threat from Russia's Kursk region was also reported, alongside confirmed Russian territorial gains near Hranove in the east. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77642, @eRadarrua/127245, @mon1tor_ua/77632, @DeepStateUA/23950)
key_points: At least three Geran-5 drones struck Kyiv's TEC-6 facility in Desnyansky district, causing power and water outages across parts of the capital. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77642)
Russian forces executed a double strike on Dnipro, damaging an electrical substation and striking near the railway station, creating a large smoke column. (Source: @eRadarrua/127245)

Dozens of reactive UAVs were tracked crossing from Sumy region through Poltava toward Kyiv and Cherkasy regions, targeting multiple towns including Romny, Buryn, Lohvytsia, and Pyriatyn. (Source: @kpszsu/91600, @kpszsu/91601, @kpszsu/91611, @eRadarrua/127300)

Geran-5 drones targeted Kyiv suburbs including Brovary, Vyshhorod, Bucha, and Bila Tserkva, with one drone reported at 200m altitude over Brovary. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77625, @mon1tor_ua/77628, @mon1tor_ua/77629, @mon1tor_ua/77639)
A ballistic missile launch threat (Iskander-M/S-300/Tsirkon) was reported from Russia's Kursk region toward Ukrainian territory. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77632)

Ukrainian air raid alerts sounded repeatedly in Kyiv overnight 30-31 October, with all-clear periods at 21:51, 22:35, 23:29, 05:07, and 06:23 local time. (Source: @eRadarrua/127267, @eRadarrua/127284, @eRadarrua/127293, @eRadarrua/127322, @eRadarrua/127323)
Russian forces advanced near Hranove in the eastern front, per updated DeepState map. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23950)
Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after a 20-day pause, hitting Samara region facilities. (Source: @UkraineNow/85004)

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces launched a coordinated multi-axis drone assault overnight 30-31 October 2026, achieving direct hits on Kyiv's critical TEC-6 thermal power plant with three Geran-5 drones that disrupted electricity and water supply to parts of the capital. Concurrently, waves of jet-powered reactive UAVs transited from Sumy and Poltava regions toward Kyiv and Cherkasy oblasts, while a double strike on Dnipro damaged a substation and the railway station. The operation coincided with a reported ballistic missile threat from Kursk region and confirmed Russian tactical gains near Hranove, indicating an escalation in both intensity and geographic scope of Russian long-range strikes. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77642, @eRadarrua/127245, @kpszsu/91600, @mon1tor_ua/77632, @DeepStateUA/23950)

points: Ukrainian air defenses engaged multiple Shahed-type drones over Kyiv, Brovary, Bila Tserkva, and Rivne, with monitoring channels reporting at least one reactive Shahed circling over Dnipro and another approaching Kremenchuk in Poltava region. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77634, @mon1tor_ua/77633, @kpszsu/91626, @mon1tor_ua/77635)

Ukrainian authorities managed the evacuation of residents from Oleshky in Kherson region, with a column of 17 buses heading to Ukraine and 4 to Russia; the Ukrainian delegation accompanied evacuees to Anapa for flights to Belarus and onward bus transport home. (Source: @UkraineNow/85009, @UkraineNow/85006)

Commander-in-Chief General-Major Mykhailo Drapatyi signed an order significantly strengthening control over military medical commissions (VLK) at territorial recruitment centers, mandating continuous monitoring of commission decisions, personal liability for fraudulent conclusions, and enhanced scrutiny for chronic conditions. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23949)

The United States approved a potential Foreign Military Sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine valued at $2.1 billion, bolstering Ukrainian air defense capabilities against ballistic and cruise missile threats. (Source: @UkraineNow/85014)

Ukrainian forces resumed strikes on Russian energy infrastructure after a 20-day hiatus, targeting oil refineries in Samara region, signaling a renewed campaign against Russian economic assets. (Source: @UkraineNow/85004)

Russian forces deployed at least 6 Geran-5 drones against Kyiv oblast targets including TEC-6 in Desnyansky district, Brovary (at 200m altitude), Vyshhorod substation, Bucha, and Bila Tserkva, with monitoring channels tracking individual drone tracks from Chernihiv and Bryansk regions. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77641, @mon1tor_ua/77639, @mon1tor_ua/77630, @mon1tor_ua/77629, @mon1tor_ua/77635)

Russian forces launched a double strike on Dnipro on 30 October 2026, first hitting an electrical substation causing a massive smoke column and power disruptions, then striking near the railway station endangering passengers and workers; emergency services and energy crews responded to both impact sites. (Source: @eRadarrua/127245)

Waves of jet-powered reactive UAVs (likely Shahed-238 variants) were launched from multiple axes: from Sumy region through Poltava toward Kyiv and Cherkasy, from Kharkiv region toward Poltava (Dykanka), and from Bryansk region into Chernihiv region, with altitudes as low as 100m near Bereznytske. (Source: @kpszsu/91600, @kpszsu/91647, @eRadarrua/127289, @eRadarrua/127278)

A ballistic missile launch threat involving Iskander-M, S-300, or Tsirkon systems was detected from Russia's Kursk region, prompting heightened alert status across northern and central Ukraine. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77632)
Russian ground forces advanced near Hranove in the eastern theater, per the latest DeepState map update, indicating continued offensive operations in Donetsk region. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23950)
Russian forces made tactical gains near Hranove in Donetsk region, per DeepState map update, suggesting ongoing pressure on Ukrainian defensive lines in the area. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23950)

Dnipro, a key logistical and industrial hub in central-eastern Ukraine, suffered a coordinated double strike on energy and transport infrastructure, damaging a substation and the railway station, which may degrade Ukrainian rear-area sustainment. (Source: @eRadarrua/127245)

Reactive UAVs were tracked over Dnipropetrovsk region, including near Magdalynivka, Vilnohirsk, Bozhedarivka, and Pavlohrad, indicating persistent Russian aerial reconnaissance and strike capability deep behind the front lines. (Source: @kpszsu/91596, @kpszsu/91620, @kpszsu/91617)

A reactive Shahed was reported circling over Dnipro city, while another targeted Kremenchuk in Poltava region, demonstrating the reach of Russian long-range drone operations into central Ukraine. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77634, @mon1tor_ua/77635)

Multiple reactive UAVs entered Ukrainian airspace from Russia's Bryansk region into Chernihiv region, with tracks reported near Nizhyn, Oster, and Berezna, and a non-reactive UAV noted near Berezna at low altitude. (Source: @eRadarrua/127273, @eRadarrua/127266, @eRadarrua/127289)

From Sumy region, waves of reactive UAVs transited through Romny and Buryn toward Poltava region, with specific tracks toward Lohvytsia, Hadiach, Pyriatyn, Kobeliaky, Shyshaky, and Lubny, indicating a northern approach vector toward Kyiv. (Source: @kpszsu/91600, @kpszsu/91614, @kpszsu/91621, @kpszsu/91642, @eRadarrua/127300)

Chernihiv region air defenses engaged UAVs near Bereznytske (flight altitude 100m) and tracked a reactive UAV from Bryansk region, while Kyiv region faced Geran-5 drones approaching from Chernihiv region toward Vyshhorod district. (Source: @eRadarrua/127278, @mon1tor_ua/77627)

Kyiv oblast experienced sustained drone pressure with Geran-5 drones targeting Brovary, Vyshhorod substation, Bucha, Bila Tserkva, and reactive UAVs approaching Borodianka, Vyshneve/Boiarka, Pereiaslav, and Yahotyn, plus a UAV circling near Hlevakha moving from Lebedivka to Dymer. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77625, @mon1tor_ua/77628, @mon1tor_ua/77629, @mon1tor_ua/77635, @kpszsu/91633, @kpszsu/91648, @kpszsu/91649, @eRadarrua/127308)

Ukrainian authorities conducted a civilian evacuation from Oleshky in Russian-occupied Kherson region, with 17 buses transporting evacuees to Ukrainian-controlled territory via Anapa, Belarus, while 4 buses moved toward Russia; Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and Russian ombudswoman Tatiana Moskalkova were present. (Source: @UkraineNow/85009, @UkraineNow/85007)

No direct combat activity in southern Ukraine was reported in the monitored messages; the primary southern development was the humanitarian evacuation coordinated between Ukrainian and Russian representatives. (Source: @UkraineNow/85009, @UkraineNow/85007)

Kyiv endured multiple air raid alerts overnight 30-31 October: alerts at 22:20, 23:23 (30 Oct), 04:17, and 06:23 (31 Oct) with all-clears at 21:51, 22:35, 23:29, 05:07, and 06:23, all driven by drone threats at yellow alert level. (Source: @eRadarrua/127276, @eRadarrua/127292, @eRadarrua/127297, @eRadarrua/127323, @eRadarrua/127267, @eRadarrua/127284, @eRadarrua/127293, @eRadarrua/127322)

At least 6 Geran-5 (Shahed-136/131) drones were simultaneously tracked targeting Kyiv oblast: one on TEC-6 (Desnyansky district), one on Vyshhorod substation, one on Brovary (200m altitude), one on Bucha, one on Bila Tserkva, and one on Rivne; monitoring channels reported 3 confirmed hits on TEC-6/power lines. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77641, @mon1tor_ua/77630, @mon1tor_ua/77639, @mon1tor_ua/77629, @mon1tor_ua/77635, @mon1tor_ua/77633, @mon1tor_ua/77642)

Dozens of jet-powered reactive UAVs (likely Shahed-238) penetrated northern and central Ukraine: from Sumy region through Poltava toward Kyiv and Cherkasy, from Kharkiv region toward Poltava, from Bryansk region into Chernihiv region, with specific tracks over Romny, Buryn, Lohvytsia, Hadiach, Pyriatyn, Kobeliaky, Shyshaky, Lubny, Khorol, and across the Chornobyl exclusion zone toward western Kyiv region. (Source: @kpszsu/91600, @kpszsu/91601, @kpszsu/91611, @kpszsu/91645, @kpszsu/91646, @kpszsu/91647, @kpszsu/91650, @eRadarrua/127306, @eRadarrua/127289)

Reactive UAVs were observed over Dnipropetrovsk region near Magdalynivka, Vilnohirsk, Bozhedarivka, Pavlohrad, and Kamianetske, with one circling over Dnipro city and another approaching Kremenchuk, indicating a broad front of aerial penetration. (Source: @kpszsu/91596, @kpszsu/91620, @kpszsu/91617, @kpszsu/91626, @mon1tor_ua/77634, @mon1tor_ua/77635)

A UAV circled near Hlevakha (Kyiv region) moving from Lebedivka to Dymer, and another circled over Kyiv at high altitude, suggesting possible reconnaissance or loitering munition tactics. (Source: @eRadarrua/127308, @eRadarrua/127318)

sections.threat_assessment: The overnight operation demonstrates a significant escalation in Russian long-range strike capacity, combining massed Geran-5 attacks on critical energy infrastructure in Kyiv with widespread reactive UAV penetration across northern and central Ukraine. The simultaneous threat of ballistic missile launches from Kursk region adds a high-speed dimension that could overwhelm air defenses during drone saturation. The double strike on Dnipro's energy and transport nodes suggests a deliberate campaign to degrade Ukrainian logistics and industrial resilience. Russian tactical gains near Hranove indicate continued ground pressure that may be synchronized with aerial interdiction. Ukrainian air defenses face a multi-layered threat requiring prioritized allocation of limited interceptor stocks.
